correctness.rationale: For a proper selected set \(D\), the complement of a complete multipartite graph is connected exactly when it is a singleton or meets at least two parts. Domination holds exactly when \(D\) meets at least two parts or equals one entire part. These biconditionals give three disjoint failure families: the empty set; a nonempty proper subset of one part; and sets whose complement has at least two vertices contained in one part. Subtracting their cardinality-generating functions from \((1+x)^N\) gives the displayed polynomial, and evaluation at \(x=1\) simplifies to the stated total. The frozen verifier independently checks literal domination/connectivity and every coefficient over all part profiles through order ten; arbitrary order rests on the symbolic proof.
